instructions.title: How to use Hash Generator

steps.title: Enter your text or drop a file
steps.description: Type or paste text in the input area, drag & drop a file for file hashing, or switch to bulk mode for multiple inputs at once.

steps.title: Choose your algorithm and mode
steps.description: Select a hash algorithm (SHA-256, SHA-512, MD5, etc.) and choose between standard hash or HMAC mode for keyed authentication.

steps.title: Configure options
steps.description: Optionally add a salt (prepend or append), set an HMAC key, or change the output format (hex, uppercase hex, or Base64).

steps.title: Copy or compare results
steps.description: Copy individual hashes, copy all at once, or use Compare Mode to verify a hash against your input. The tool auto-detects hash type from length.

features: Six algorithms: SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384, SHA-1, MD5, CRC32
HMAC support for SHA-based keyed authentication
File hashing with drag & drop and progress indicator
Bulk mode: hash multiple strings in one go
Output formats: hex lowercase, hex uppercase, Base64
Auto-detect hash type from pasted hash length
Salt support with prepend or append position
Security warnings for deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA-1)
useCases: Verify file integrity after download (checksum verification)
Generate HMAC signatures for API authentication
Compare checksums of ISO images or software packages
Verify data integrity across network transfers
Create unique identifiers from text content
proTips: Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 for security-sensitive hashing — MD5 and SHA-1 are broken
Always use HMAC (not salt + hash) when authenticating messages with a secret key
Drag & drop large files — the tool processes them in chunks with a progress bar
Paste any hash in Compare Mode and the tool auto-detects its algorithm
Use Base64 output format when working with JWT or web-based systems
Bulk mode accepts one input per line — perfect for hashing word lists or URLs
troubleshooting: File hashing slow: Large files are processed in 2MB chunks — wait for the progress bar to complete
HMAC unavailable for MD5/CRC32: HMAC uses the Web Crypto API which only supports SHA algorithms
Hash mismatch: Check encoding — the same string in UTF-8 vs Latin-1 produces different hashes
Compare Mode shows no match: Ensure both hashes use the same format (hex vs Base64)
Browser compatibility: SHA hashing requires a modern browser with Web Crypto API support

ui.infoText: Cryptographic hash functions produce a fixed-size output from any input. The same input always produces the same hash, but it's computationally infeasible to reverse.
ui.hmacInfoText: HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) uses a secret key to produce an authenticated hash. Used for API signatures, webhook verification, and message authentication.
